Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

order verb

tell someone to do something

also command, bid, tell someone to, give an order, give orders

classical

Caes. BG 1.27: eōs suum adventum exspectāre jussit (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 9.13.2: hae mē litterae Dolābellae jubent ad prīstinās cōgitātiōnēs revertī (Lewis & Short)

jubeō, jubēre, jussī, jussum

verb, second conjugation; with the accusative and infinitive

order, tell (someone to do something)

The ordinary verb: the person told stands in the accusative, what is to be done in the infinitive. Also of what the people enact: senātus dēcrēvit populusque jussit (Cic. Verr. 2.2.161, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • imperō, imperāre, imperāvī, imperātum — command, give an order

    verb, first conjugation; with the dative of the person and ut or nē with the subjunctive · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.28.1: hīs, utī conquīrerent et redūcerent, imperāvit (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 2.32.3: quae imperārentur, facere dīxērunt (Lewis & Short)

    The command of someone in authority: a general, a master, a parent.

Examples

  • eōs suum adventum exspectāre jussit

    he ordered them to wait for his arrivalCaes. BG 1.27 (Lewis & Short)

  • hīs, utī conquīrerent et redūcerent, imperāvit

    he ordered them to hunt the men out and bring them backCaes. BG 1.28.1 (Lewis & Short)

  • quae imperārentur, facere dīxērunt

    they said they would do what was orderedCaes. BG 2.32.3 (Lewis & Short)

See also command, rule, command.
